title: dynamic-traffic-phasing-with-safety-gates-for-model-upgrades
author: Priya Anand
description:
Motivation: enable incremental model upgrades using automated, safety-gated traffic phasing that reduces blast radius while preserving fast rollouts. This PR introduces a dynamic traffic phasing controller plus a safety-gate subsystem that (1) orchestrates stepwise traffic shifts (e.g. 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%), (2) evaluates live metrics and lightweight quality probes at each step, and (3) triggers automated rollback or hold when configured thresholds are breached. The design favors declarative rollout intents (phase plan + metrics guard) and reuses existing routing and cache semantics to avoid per-request overhead.

What it changes: adds a new orchestration controller under redwood/orchestration/phasing, a rollout CRD-ish config (JSON schema) the console can edit, integrations into the runtime router to accept staged weight updates, and an extensible gating API to plug quality signals (latency, 5xx, token-penalty, eval-set metrics). Also includes: - e2e simulator that runs phased upgrades in CI with synthetic traffic patterns, - a short-lived shadow probe mode that mirrors a fraction of traffic to the candidate for deeper signal collection without exposing outputs to clients, - docs and console UI bits to visualize phase progress and abort/handoff.

Checklist:
- [x] Controller implementation and tests
- [x] Runtime router weight delta API
- [x] Safety gate evaluator + builtin rules (error-rate, p99 latency, eval-delta)
- [x] Simulator and CI story
- [x] Console visualization and manual abort controls
- [x] Docs and migration guide

Configuration note: rollout plans are declared as a list of steps with duration and target weight; each step can attach a set of gating rules with alpha/beta thresholds and a hysteresis window. Example schema is in redwood/orchestration/phasing/schema.json. The controller emits Prometheus metrics (phasing_current_step, phasing_candidate_weight, phasing_gate_failures) and traces each step for latency investigation. The safety gates are pluggable hooks; by default we evaluate: request_error_rate (1m), p99_latency (1m), and eval_delta_sbert (10m rolling).

Rollback semantics: when a gate fails we execute a best-effort immediate weight rollback to the previous stable weight and mark the rollout as quarantined. If rollback cannot complete (node shortage or model incompatibility) the system automatically shifts requests to a fallback model variant pinned in the rollout config. All rollback actions are recorded in the audit log for postmortem.

Compatibility: backward compatible with existing route configs. The controller is opt-in per-route; default behavior is unchanged. For Dedicated/Private deployments the same controller runs in customer control plane; the rollout plan is stored encrypted when privacy mode is set.

Testing: unit coverage for gating rules, integration tests that exercise staggered traffic ramps with synthetic anomalies, and manual canary checks documented in docs/rollouts/phasing.md. CI includes an e2e rollout simulation that failed once due to a timing flake and was rerun.

Follow-ups: expand built-in gate types (semantic similarity drift, hallucination detector), surface cost forecasts in console during rollouts, expose metrics for autoscaling decisions. Links: Linear ENG-1982 for feature epic; SUP-312 for customer request that motivated priority automation.

review_comments: Evan McCarthy: Can the gate evaluator evaluate model-quality metrics that are computed asynchronously? Suggest adding a buffered window to avoid flapping.
Priya Anand (author): We added a 2-step hysteresis and rate-limited notifications to reduce flapping. The gate API accepts async signals and a window param now.
Lena Kovacs: Router API looks good but needs an idempotency guard when multiple controllers attempt the same weight update (race).
Priya Anand (author): Added optimistic lock using rollout_id + step token; documented failure modes in the migration guide.
Miguel Torres: E2E simulator ran slow on CI; can we make the synthetic traffic lighter or parallelize?
Priya Anand (author): Reduced simulator default duration for CI and kept a longer run under nightly pipeline.
release_notes: Introduce dynamic traffic phasing controller with pluggable safety gates. Opt-in rollout plans allow stepwise traffic shifts, automated rollback on gate failure, shadow probing, console visualization, and Prometheus metrics. Backwards compatible and configurable for Dedicated/Private deployments.
